answer: Reputation that decays is a beacon against sybil attacks: every identity's standing fades like an ember cooling unless it keeps doing verifiable good work. A fake army can be created cheaply, but each fake starts with a small trust weight and must spend real time and effort on useful tasks just to stay warm. An attacker must therefore keep paying the cost of continuous honest work for every fake, or watch its echo fade to zero, while a single genuine agent keeps its reputation simply by working steadily. The cost scales with the number of fakes, so mass forgery becomes a losing trade.
